pr_title: Fix incorrect r2r codegen for hardware instrinsics
pr_body:
Use of Vector dot product and Vector3/4 constructors may generate code that is not compatible with an SSE2 capable CPU.

This fix adjusts the set of rules for filtering the intrinsics when compiling System.Private.CoreLib, and makes the behavior in crossgen2 match that of crossgen1.

Fixes #32175
pr_comments: I spoke to @AntonLapounov offline and got signoff.

issue_context.title: crossgen2 codegen for with AVX instructions differs from crossgen1 generated one
issue_context.body:
In both cases, the code was compiled with optimizations on.
One example of part of code of a method with such a difference is `System.Numerics.Matrix4x4 System.Numerics.Matrix4x4.CreateConstrainedBillboard(System.Numerics.Vector3, System.Numerics.Vector3, System.Numerics.Vector3, System.Numerics.Vector3, System.Numerics.Vector3)`:
Crossgen1:
```asm
    movaps xmm1, xmm0
    dpps xmm1, xmm0, 113
    movss xmm2, dword ptr [0x7ec50]
    ucomiss xmm2, xmm1
    jbe 0x007D
```
Crossgen2:
```asm
    movaps xmm2, xmm0
    mulps xmm2, xmm0
    movaps xmm1, xmm2
    shufps xmm1, xmm1, 129
    addps xmm2, xmm1
    shufps xmm1, xmm1, 15
    addps xmm2, xmm1
    movss xmm1, dword ptr [0x13cba0]
    ucomiss xmm1, xmm2
    jbe 0x008B
```
There are more differences in the body of the method, this is just a small example.
comments: Here is a gist with full disass of the method for crossgen 1 and 2: https://gist.github.com/janvorli/e80da2329748dc15a23a445246c65028
This is actually a bug in crossgen 1. It should be generating the longer sequence instead of the dpps instruction.

There is also a similar bug in crossgen 1 around use of the insertps instruction, and plausible future bugs around min, max and abs.

There are bugs in the crossgen2 compilation in that popcnt isn't generated directly. (In particular, the SSE41, SSE42 and POPCNT instructions aren't marked as eligible for the jit to generate for corelib). This both causes the `popcnt` bug in crossgen2, and causes the bugs noted here where we incorrectly generate `insertps` and `dpps` into the R2R for System.Private.CoreLib.
Also issue with `Vector128<byte>.Zero` which remains a call at crossgen https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/32714

> Or is this "correct-by-design" behavior?

This is by design right now (in CoreLib only). AVX2 support is a global switch in RyuJIT - it enables VEX encoding everywhere (including outside the IsSupported-guarded regions). We can't allow RyuJIT to use it because it would generate code that cannot run without VEX.

Outside CoreLib, using VEX2 instructions in the method body would disqualify the method from crossgenning completely. Within corelib, we still pregenerate the code, but with VEX disabled. This is because VEX intrinsics are used in code paths that are parts of the startup path and we don't want to JIT them every time we start.

ReadyToRun is a startup optimization, not a throughput optimization. Similar restrictions apply to other ReadyToRun code - the code is not ideal by design (e.g. it needs to be version resilient) - we need reJIT to achieve optimal throughput.

I'm working on adding an ability to specify to crossgen2 the minimal instruction set support, and hopefully that will allow the faster code to kick in more quickly for more scenarios, but the current model is that for CoreLib ONLY, Avx2.IsSupported will return false from the R2R code, and will change to true when it is re-tiered. (This requires your code to work in such a situation, we decided we could code review changes to CoreLib to make this safe.). For non-CoreLib, we simply disable generation of the code in crossgen entirely, and rely on the jit which has unfortunate startup time effects.)

> > Or is this "correct-by-design" behavior?
> 
> This is by design right now (in CoreLib only). AVX2 support is a global switch in RyuJIT - it enables VEX encoding everywhere (including outside the IsSupported-guarded regions). We can't allow RyuJIT to use it because it would generate code that cannot run without VEX.

Thanks I read up on the crazy state transitions in various Intel processors w.r.t to this issue and I now completely understand why you must disallow this when targeting SSE2.

review_comments: Why doesn't this logic apply to R2R? Isn't it supposed to be the CPUID caching/checking logic for R2R/Crossgen?

Things outside READYTORUN are used in CoreRT. CoreRT doesn't block pregeneration of `Vector<T>` like crossgen2 does (it can't, because it's AOT) - AFAIK enabling SSE4.X would result in Vector using them. So they're known at compile time as never supported.

Maybe it would be better to delete this code and make `HardwareIntrinsicHelpers` a partial class instead so that it doesn't distract within the shipping product.

That seems like something that should be handled in the `Compiler::getSIMDSupportLevel()` check, rather than something which blocks `if (Sse41.IsSupported) { }` from being compiled down to a cached CPUID check like SSE3 and the others have happen.
Substantial engineering for CoreRT is not budgeted for at this time. The current logic works well enough, and while I agree in the long term this isn't ideal, it should work for now.
A bit below at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/33090/files#diff-2ff7a6ceb92854abf02ee2e4eb4b657eR102, but this seems to be missing the code paths for SSE4.1, SSE4.2, and POPCNT?
This is for the non R2R case, where the exact behavior is known (disabled).

This might be more of a question for Tanner, but would it make sense to introduce some mechanism on JitInterface to express this? It already felt a bit ugly when this was just Round and it seems like we missed another place - feels like this could be a problem again in the future when RyuJIT finds a new place to use these ISA extensions.

What if instead of the EE side specifying what ISA extensions are allowed before compiling a method, RyuJIT would ask EE side whenever it would like to use it instead and include a reason (HW intrinsic class normally guarded by an `IsSupported` check, or an opportunistic optimization of an existing API)?

This kind of contract would potentially make it easier to introduce multi-versioning later (right now the crossgen2 driver side has no way of knowing whether multiple versions even make sense).

Not sure if it's a good idea - just trying to find a way to avoid this fragility because I don't think anyone is really happy about it.

I think the issue only exists today for S.P.Corelib, because we have methods which we might optimize internally and therefore cannot easily express the different code paths to the JIT (functionally it is an `IsSupported` check, but not one codified in the IR trees, which I believe is the root problem).

All of these checks are under `Compiler::compSupports(ISA)` (HWIntrinsics and other opts) or `Compiler::getSIMDSupportLevel()` (SIMDIntrinsics) calls, so it might be possible to tweak that code path to just return `false` for any non-baseline code path if we are in R2R or Crossgen mode.

I'd like to think about a more complex instruction compatibility story, and in fact notification from RyuJit across the jit interface when a more interesting instruction is used, but I want to reserve that sort of change for future work. This is fixing a targetted problem. Once this is fixed, I can go after a more ambitious work experiment in that direction. As part of the instruction-set feature for crossgen2 I intend to build support for noting which functions are taking advantage of what instruction sets, and possibly enable/disable R2R function use on a per method basis, but that's going to require a fair bit more research.

For `compSupports`, it looks like we are correctly handling all the cases (`Math.Round` and various `Vector128/256` helper methods, such as `WithElement`).
For `getSIMDSupportLevel` around `SIMD_SSE4_Supported`, it looks like there might be a couple cases (such as Equality/Inequality, Min/Max) and a couple asserts that might need further investigation.

So far, of the `getSIMDSupportLevel` cases, they all look to be scenarios where we aren't utilizing such code in S.P.Corelib directly, so it isn't currently a problem.

For example, multiplication for `Vector<int>` is only supported on SSE4.1 and above: <https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/coreclr/src/jit/simdcodegenxarch.cpp#L209>
or `Vector<T>` equality/inequality against constant `0` will generate `ptest: <https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/coreclr/src/jit/simdcodegenxarch.cpp#L2045>

But, the S.N.Vector methods aren't recursive and so this only presents itself (like in the `DotProduct` case), when some other code in S.P.Corelib is calling one of these methods.
Why are these 3 supported under Ready2Run but not under other scenarios? Is the other path here for Crossgen1/2?
The other path is for CoreRT, which isn't a crossgen scenario at all. (And really shouldn't be in this repo, but the current amount of CoreRT logic embedded in here isn't really large.)
It being for CoreRT was where I was getting confused. Thanks for clarifying!
Is there a way to assert that this is always true?
Also a bit below at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/33090/files#diff-2ff7a6ceb92854abf02ee2e4eb4b657eR170, how are SSE4.1, SSE4.2, and POPCNT known at compile time?
This is for the non R2R case, where the exact behavior is known (disabled).
